author: Grandfather Ulf, who has outlived three wolves and a bear
pages:
#Before You Leave the Road

The wilds do not want to kill you. They simply do not care whether you live. Most deaths in the wilderness come not from monsters but from cold, falls and bad decisions made when tired.

Rest before you are exhausted. Eat before you are starving. Turn back before you are lost.

#Wolves and Bears

Wolves hunt in packs and test you from several sides at once. Keep your back to a rock or tree and they can only come at you from the front. Bears are solitary and terrifying, but they would rather eat berries than travellers. Give them room.

Sabre-toothed cats give no warning and no quarter. If you see one, it has already decided.

#Trolls

A troll will heal its wounds almost as fast as you can give them. Only fire stops the healing. Carry a torch, a fire spell, or a very fast pair of legs.

#Giants

Giants are not usually hostile. They tend their mammoths and keep to themselves. If you approach their camp, they will warn you off by stamping and roaring. Take the hint. A giant's club can send a grown warrior into the sky, and the landing is the part that kills.

#The Most Dangerous Creature

The most dangerous creature in the north is the traveller who thinks he has nothing left to learn. I have buried several. Do not be the next.
